steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another — e.g. £1 = $1.25. Determined by supply and demand in the foreign exchange market.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Appreciation: pound becomes stronger (buys more foreign currency). Depreciation: pound becomes weaker (buys less).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Appreciation: imports cheaper (good for consumers), exports more expensive (bad for UK exporters), overseas holidays cheaper.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Depreciation: imports more expensive (inflationary), exports cheaper (boosting export demand), overseas holidays cost more.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Appreciation = stronger currency. Depreciation = weaker currency. Don't confuse them. Appreciation: imports cheaper, exports dearer. Depreciation: imports dearer, exports cheaper. Always consider the effect on BOTH consumers and producers.
